Stars: single NULL star.updated row breaks all star reads/writes for that user (500 "expected stars object")

**What happened?**

For one specific user, every dashboard star operation fails: clicking the star icon returns HTTP 500, and the "Starred" section of the nav renders empty even though the user has valid star rows in the database. Other users on the same instance are unaffected.

Log output for the failing user:

```
logger=grafana-apiserver level=error msg="Unhandled Error" err="apiserver received an error that is not an metav1.Status: &errors.errorString{s:\"expected stars object\"}: expected stars object"
logger=context userId=2 level=error msg="Request Completed" method=POST path=/api/user/stars/dashboard/uid/business-kpis status=500 error="expected stars object"
```

**Root cause**

The `star` table schema declares `updated` as nullable (`updated DATETIME NULL`), but the collections API's legacy bridge scans it into a bare `time.Time`:

`pkg/registry/apis/collections/legacy/sql.go`, in `getDashboardStars`:

```
var updated time.Time
...
err := rows.Scan(&orgID, &userUID, &dashboardUID, &updated)
```

A single row with `updated = NULL` makes this `Scan` fail. Because `sql_dashboard_stars.sql` orders by `s.updated asc` and SQLite sorts NULLs first, the poisoned row is scanned first, so `getDashboardStars` fails for every call touching that user:

- `DashboardStarsStorage.Get` returns the scan error, which is not a `NotFound`
- In `stars_update.go` (`starsREST.Connect`), a non-NotFound error from `Get` leaves `current` as nil, so the `current.(*collections.Stars)` type assertion fails and the handler responds with the misleading `expected stars object` error for both PUT and DELETE
- The read path fails the same way, so the user's starred list renders empty

Net effect: one NULL in a legally-nullable column bricks the entire stars feature for that user, including the DELETE path that could have removed the offending row via the API.

NULL values in this column occur in practice: rows written by older Grafana versions or by operators backfilling `dashboard_uid` during migrations (the column was added later; the schema accepts NULL, so nothing flags the insert).

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Star any dashboard as a user
2. `UPDATE star SET updated = NULL WHERE user_id = <that user>;`
3. Reload Grafana: the starred list is empty
4. Click the star icon on any dashboard: POST /api/user/stars/dashboard/uid/... returns 500 "expected stars object"

**Suggested fix**

Scan into `sql.NullTime` in `getDashboardStars` and fall back to a zero time (the value only affects star display order). Separately, `stars_update.go` swallows the underlying error when `Get` fails with a non-NotFound error; returning that error instead of the type-assertion message would have made this diagnosable from the log alone.

**Environment**

- Grafana 13.2.0 (f681b1359f6a0b8ecb9f2c49a88ac72b75bde73b), OSS, SQLite backend, deployed via kube-prometheus-stack

Accessibility: Dynamic Heading component

Grafana components often choose heading levels locally. For example, [News](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/pull/132517/changes#diff-cd0156f48113c61b1f50b552f85098c3e7ac6324c06430473ea171916412cd9aL46-R59) used to render `h1` elements regardless of where it's used. [PanelChrome](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/main/packages/grafana-ui/src/components/PanelChrome/PanelChrome.tsx) renders `h2`

A reusable panel or component can appear at different depths in a page. It's headings need to reflect that structure, not the position the author originally expected. Fixed levels either make reuse difficult, or usability with screen-readers worse because an inaccurate hierarchy can obscure the relationships between a page, its sections, and their content. See the [WAI guidance on heading structure](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/page-structure/headings/).

Additionally - some partners embed Grafana within their page which already have their own heading levels, so Grafana re-creating its own H1 leads to more disjointed heading structures.

Add a context-aware `Heading` and `HeadingSection` primitives to `@grafana/ui`. `HeadingSection` acts as a boundary that carries and increments the heading level through React context without adding wrapping DOM elements.

- A page root establishes the initial level, normally `1`
- Each nested `HeadingSection` increments the heading level for its descendents. Sibling headings retain the same level.
- An explicit level can establish a new root for a subtree e.g. for modals/drawers/etc
- Each heading reads its level from the nearest boundary. Its visual style remains independent, similar to the existing `Text` component

Example API:

```
<HeadingRoot level={rootHeadingLevel}>
  <Heading variant="xl">Explore</Heading> {/* h1 */}

  <HeadingSection>
    <Heading variant="lg">Query pane A</Heading> {/* h2 */}

    <HeadingSection>
      <Heading variant="md">Queries</Heading> {/* h3 */}
      <QueryEditor />
    </HeadingSection>
[... 7 more lines]
```

Note: currently typography style variants are called `h1`/`h2`/`h3`. Here, to avoid confusion, I've used new names for these styles that are being proposed separately.

Instead of needing to explicitly give headings a level (which may not be portable depending on the usage), or pass heading levels through components, their nesting inside `<HeadingSection>`s automatically set the level.

We use native `h1`-`h6` elements. For deeper nesting we _could_ use `role="heading"` and `aria-level={7+}` _if_ we validate that supported screen readers support this.

- [Ariakit: HeadingLevel](https://ariakit.com/reference/heading-level) provides DOM-free, automatically incrementing boundaries.
- [Carbon: Section and Heading](https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon/blob/main/packages/react/src/components/Heading/Heading.mdx) combine section markup with automatic heading levels.
- [Atlaskit: Heading](https://atlassian.design/components/heading/) separates typography from inherited levels and supports ARIA headings beyond level 6.

Table: power column sorting from the ad-hoc stage, and persist sort as a panel transformation

Current prototype: #133050. Closed working PR #132542 below is historical context, not shipped implementation.

Sorting is the interesting one, because unlike reorder and hide it already has a persisted home: `onSortByChange` writes `options.sortBy` ([public/app/features/table/utils.ts](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/main/public/app/features/table/utils.ts)).

Moving it onto the ad-hoc stage (https://github.com/grafana/grafana/pull/132542) means migrating that panel option to a `sortBy` **transformation saved on the panel**, so that sorting-then-saving persists a panel transformation rather than a panel option.

**The consequence, stated plainly:** until a **promote-transformations** workflow exists — an editor saving the currently applied ad-hoc stage into the dashboard — that migration *removes* the ability to persist a sort on save. That is a real, temporary regression, and it is why sorting was not moved in #132542. The migration should land with, or after, promote.

**Also needed:** a schema migration path for the existing `options.sortBy` in [public/app/plugins/panel/table/migrations.ts](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/main/public/app/plugins/panel/table/migrations.ts).

This supersedes the old long-tail proposal to persist sorting to `fieldConfig`: the proposed persisted representation is a panel transformation. Existing saved sorting must remain functional throughout migration.

Part of grafana/grafana-org#1000. Depends on the ad-hoc foundation (#133138) and sharing/promotion (#133139).

Design doc: [Table Ad-Hoc Transformations](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ixPSx2-vh6-6PUFMcFAKddoKICqPvwCYYyXzFzHHWQU/edit)

Table: column pinning

Current prototype: #133050. Closed working PR #132542 and branch #130506 below are historical context, not shipped implementation. The approach below remains a proposal; pinning's representation is not settled. Sharing/promotion is tracked in #133139.

Column pinning is the one refreshed-table column interaction left out of the ad-hoc transformation stage (https://github.com/grafana/grafana/pull/132542), because it is the only one that isn't purely a data change.

A pin is two things at once:

- a **reorder** — pinned columns have to form a leading run, because react-data-grid only freezes a leading run
- a **panel-option change** — the frozen column count, `frozenColumns.left`

Only the first half is expressible as `organize`. Shipping just that half would be lossy (unpinning has no memory of the prior order) and would leak a purely visual affordance into everything downstream that reads the post-ad-hoc frames — CSV download, Inspect Data.

**Proposed approach:** a "hidden" transformation type whose effect is to tweak panel options and which is deliberately not listed in the transformations UI. A pin then becomes a single ad-hoc entry carrying both halves. The same mechanism is what brings the persisted `sortBy` option into reach (see the sorting issue).

**Open questions for that design:**

- How does such a type interact with the transformations editors' wholesale-replace model, once it can be promoted into `panel.transformations`?
- Can an options-mutating transformation be made idempotent enough to re-run on every pipeline pass?

**Also in scope:** adding `pinnable` to `TableFieldOptions` alongside `filterable` / `sortable` / `reorderable` / `hideable`. It was deliberately left out of #132542 so it could be built against real behaviour rather than added speculatively.

The pin UI already exists on the working branch (https://github.com/grafana/grafana/pull/130506) — the handler is simply not passed, which takes the menu item with it. Two things that come back with it: seeding the pinned set from the column catalog rather than the post-hide fields, and pruning pinned names on reconciliation instead of wiping them.

Depends on the shared ad-hoc foundation in #133138. Part of grafana/grafana-org#1000.

Design doc: [Table Ad-Hoc Transformations](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ixPSx2-vh6-6PUFMcFAKddoKICqPvwCYYyXzFzHHWQU/edit)

Allow disabling alerting for a data source so it cannot be used to create alert rules

`jsonData.manageAlerts: false` does not actually prevent a data source from being used
to create alert rules. There is no working, reliable way to disable alerting for a data
source from the UI.

The data source config editor exposes a "Manage alert rules in Alerting UI" switch that
is backed by `jsonData.manageAlerts` (`AlertingSettings` in `packages/grafana-ui`).
The expectation is that turning this switch off fully disables alert management for the
data source, so users can no longer create or edit alert rules against it.

In practice, `jsonData.manageAlerts: false` only affects external rules sources:
`isDataSourceManagingAlerts` / `getRulesDataSources`
(`public/app/features/alerting/unified/utils/datasource.ts`) filter the list of external
(Prometheus/Loki-flavored) rules sources. It does **not** stop a user from manually
creating a Grafana-managed alert rule whose query targets that data source through the
Alerting UI.

This matters when a data source is meant to be managed outside Grafana. A concrete case
is the VictoriaLogs data source
([victorialogs-datasource](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/victorialogs-datasource)):
logs-based alerts are often managed externally via `VMRule` + `vmalert` using LogsQL,
with Grafana acting only as a read-only client. See
[victorialogs-datasource#727](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/victorialogs-datasource/issues/727).
Even with `jsonData.manageAlerts: false`, a user can still manually create a
VictoriaLogs-backed alert rule in the UI, which can produce expensive LogsQL rules that
are hard to review and put continuous load on VictoriaLogs.

`jsonData.manageAlerts: false` should fully disable alert creation for the data source,
but it does not. Concretely:

- Provisioning a data source with `jsonData.manageAlerts: false` still allows manually
  creating an alert rule for that data source via the Alerting UI.
- There is no setting that reliably prevents a data source from being chosen as the query
  target of a Grafana-managed alert rule.

Provide a way to fully disable alerting for a data source from the UI, such that:

- The "Manage alert rules in Alerting UI" toggle, when off, prevents the data source from
  being used to create or edit any alert rule (both data source-managed and Grafana-managed).
- This behavior should also apply to any data source that opts out of alerting, regardless
  of whether its `plugin.json` declares `alerting: true`.

Graphite query editor intermittently throws a TypeError when editing alert rules

Opening or editing an alert rule with a Graphite query can intermittently produce:

```
TypeError: Cannot set properties of undefined (setting 'target')
```

The stack points to `public/app/plugins/datasource/graphite/state/store.ts:77`, where the query-change action assigns `state.target.target`.

Production logs show the error primarily on `/alerting/*/edit` routes, across multiple Grafana versions. The earliest occurrence found in the sampled history was July 1, 2026, on `13.2.0-28013533988`.

In a six-hour window on September 7, 2026 (03:22–09:22 UTC), there were 42 matching errors across 18 sessions. Graphite function-loading and metric-discovery requests around sampled failures returned HTTP 200. Sessions without the error had comparable request durations, so request latency alone does not explain the failures.

Some affected sessions continued issuing rule-test and rule-save requests afterward. We have not established whether those saves succeeded or whether the error consistently blocks editing.

A React-level reproduction triggers the error by delaying Graphite initialization and re-rendering with a cloned query object—even when the query text is unchanged.

The sequence is:

1. Graphite initializes its editor store asynchronously.
2. A time-range update can publish partial state containing `range` but no `target`.
3. A subsequent query-prop update dispatches `queryChanged`.
4. That action accesses the missing `state.target` and throws.

This sequence is consistent with the production logs, but the precise production re-render that triggers it remains unconfirmed.

The Graphite editor should safely accept query and time-range updates while loading and preserve the latest values without throwing.

Streaming: grafana live stream panels randomly fail with "Streaming channel error: Expired"

sometimes a live-streaming panel gets stuck with:

`Streaming channel error: expired`

i can reproduce/observe this when changing the dashboard time interval, then changing it back to a time interval/query that was used before.

in my case, the datasource includes the time interval in the Grafana Live channel path, so for example:
`now-5m-now` -> `now-15m-now` -> `now-5m-now`

when switching back, the channel path becomes identical to one that was already used earlier. after that, Grafana sometimes shows the stale `expired` stream error until i refresh/reload the dashboard.

i checked the Grafana source and the error seems to come from the Grafana Live/Centrifuge frontend path:

- `public/app/features/live/centrifuge/channel.ts` stores `ctx.error.message` from Centrifuge subscription errors
- `public/app/features/live/centrifuge/LiveDataStream.ts` emits `Streaming channel error: ${err.message}`
- `public/app/features/live/centrifuge/service.ts` caches `LiveDataStream` instances by channel id

so this looks like a stale cached live stream/channel state being reused when subscribing again to a previously used path.

when a query subscribes again to a previously used live channel path, Grafana should either create a clean live stream state or clear/retry transient Centrifuge errors.

a previous `expired` state should not be replayed to the panel as a fresh query error.

the panel should recover without needing a dashboard refresh/reload.

Embeddable resources: generic embeddings and hybrid search

Make manifest-declared resources embeddable and hybrid-searchable through Grafana's existing unified-storage embedding pipeline. Dashboard extraction and hybrid ranking already exist; this work adds generic resource support and migrates the dashboard caller to the shared API.

The SDK declaration work is complete in https://github.com/grafana/grafana-app-sdk/pull/1541. Grafana's dependency upgrade will wait for a release containing that PR.

- Declare embedding inputs independently of search fields, under each API version's `embed.fields`. These fields generate embedding text; they do not enable filtering by those fields.
- Resolve input paths using each object's stored `apiVersion`, including historical unserved versions. Different versions may use different paths.
- Keep one manual `embed[resource].reembedVersion` per resource across all API versions. Input edits alone do not require a bump; increasing the number intentionally requests re-embedding through the existing version machinery.
- Custom builders, including dashboards, own their version in Go and omit both declarative embedding inputs and the root embedding configuration entry.
- Reuse `vector_allowed_internal_collections` as the single resource allowlist for both generation and query access. Existing global indexing/provider settings continue to apply; preserve today's dashboard defaults.
- Mount the generic hybrid endpoint from `search.hybrid` and the API server's `enable_hybrid_api` switch. Route mounting does not depend on storage-server configuration. Generic filtering initially supports UID/folder; existing dashboard-specific filters remain dashboard-specific.
- Reuse existing reconciliation, deletion, content-version backfills and provider batching support. Keep storage-server support and API-layer changes in separate PRs/deployments, with compatibility during version skew.

The enrollment sub-issue contains two implementation stages suitable for separate PRs: configuration/builder selection, followed by catalog provisioning and storage execution.

The generic builder, backfill page batching, and generic hybrid API contract can start while the SDK release is pending. The builder can initially use an unwired provider interface.

After the release, land the SDK/provider integration and storage enrollment support. Roll out storage support before enabling the API routes. Use a resource fully in unified storage for the first end-to-end rollout. Migrate the command palette in a separate frontend PR; retire the old dashboard endpoint only after deployed clients have moved.

- An enrolled generic resource can backfill existing objects, process new writes/updates/deletes, and serve authorized hybrid queries.
- Tests cover different paths across stored API versions, historical unserved versions, custom-builder precedence, manual version increases, and safe skips when declarations are missing. Missing declarations preserve existing embeddings.
- Generation and query access use the single agreed allowlist. Unsupported/disallowed requests fail before consuming provider quota.
- Existing dashboard behavior and older API/storage combinations remain compatible through rollout.
- The first generic-resource rollout is verified, the command palette uses the generic API, and the legacy dashboard endpoint is retired after migration.

Keep the current event-triggered initial backfill: the first processed write, including an eligible replayed write, initializes a resource's backfill job. A quiet newly enrolled resource is not guaranteed an immediate backfill. Guaranteed bootstrap on enrollment and durable recovery of missed backfill events remain follow-ups.

Other deferred work includes automatic embedding-definition hashes, mandatory identical declarations across API versions, arbitrary filtering on embedding inputs, generic document chunking, and automatic cleanup of retained vector rows on unenrollment.

Databricks: intermittently fails with "access token is expired" due to a token-refresh timing gap

Datasources using Azure OBO (On-Behalf-Of) authentication, confirmed for Databricks, intermittently fail queries with `failed to get access token: unable to acquire access token: access token is expired`, for a period recurring roughly hourly.

**Root cause:**
Grafana holds the user's Azure sign-in token valid until 10 seconds before its actual expiry. Microsoft's MSAL library independently refuses to use any cached token with less than 5 minutes of life left ([source](https://github.com/AzureAD/microsoft-authentication-library-for-go/blob/v1.7.2/apps/internal/base/storage/items.go#L139)). This creates a window, up to several minutes wide, where Grafana still considers the sign-in token valid but MSAL rejects the downstream token as expired, so every query fails until the next refresh cycle.

**Suggested fix:**
Move the Databricks OBO exchange onto the same Azure SDK library Azure Monitor already uses, which doesn't have MSAL's 5-minute rejection behavior.

**Additional note:**
The same user that encountered this issue also reported 403 errors when accessing the Unity Catalog. They are potentially related, as an invalid token would explain a 4xx error. The user also confirmed that calling the Unity Catalog API directly does not cause any 403, suggesting that this is a plugin issue.

Configurable datasource HTTP connection refresh for DNS-based HA failover

**Why is this needed**:

Grafana alerting can continue querying an unhealthy datasource IP after a DNS-based HA endpoint removes that target.

We run Grafana with the Helm chart on Kubernetes. The HA endpoint performs periodic liveness checks and DNS returns only healthy target IPs. When a target fails, it is removed from DNS, but Grafana can continue to use an already-established HTTP connection to the old IP. Reloading or updating the datasource rebuilds its HTTP transport and recovers connectivity.

Grafana’s default data-proxy transport reuses connections. `idle_conn_timeout_seconds` defaults to 90 seconds, but only closes connections that are idle. Frequently evaluated alert rules can keep a connection eligible for reuse indefinitely, so no new TCP dial or DNS lookup occurs.

Grafana does not maintain a configurable DNS-record cache. In Kubernetes, new lookups normally use the pod resolver configuration, through CoreDNS and then the configured upstream DNS. CoreDNS and upstream DNS caches or TTLs may delay a fresh answer, but they cannot help while Grafana is reusing an existing TCP connection.

**What would you like to be added**:

Add an experimental, opt-in configuration for the maximum age of Grafana-managed datasource HTTP transports or connections.

After the configured interval, Grafana should replace the cached datasource HTTP transport and close its idle connections. Subsequent datasource requests would create a new TCP connection and perform DNS resolution again, allowing Grafana to observe the healthy target currently returned by cluster DNS and the HA DNS service.

Suggested behavior:

- Feature toggle, disabled by default, such as `datasourceHttpTransportRefresh`.
- Global `[dataproxy]` configuration, such as:

```
# 0 disables periodic transport rotation.
http_transport_refresh_interval_seconds = 0
```

- Documented and validated lower and upper bounds, for example 10 to 3600 seconds.
- Applies to Grafana-managed HTTP datasource traffic, including unified-alerting datasource queries.
- Does not override DNS TTLs or implement a Grafana DNS cache.
- Does not change existing behavior when disabled.

This would make the maximum delay before Grafana observes an HA DNS failover more predictable:

```
HA liveness detection time
+ DNS TTL / CoreDNS cache time
+ Grafana transport refresh interval
```

**Who is this feature for?**

Grafana operators using DNS-based high availability or failover for HTTP datasources, especially Prometheus-compatible systems and other endpoints whose healthy target IP can change at runtime.

It is particularly important for operators running unified alerting, where frequent rule evaluations keep datasource HTTP connections active and stale connections can affect alert reliability.

Series/cardinality count per metric row

Show a count per metric row in the datasource explorer sidebar — the `4.8k` / `1.9k` / `402` values in the mockup.

Split out of grafana/grafana#128774, which delivered metric loading, lazy-loading and row expansion. The count was the one bullet of that ticket that could not be delivered alongside them, so it was blocking grafana/grafana#128774 from closing.

**1. A product decision (Kirby): what is that number?**

* **Cardinality** — how many series the metric has. Expensive, and there is no cheap source today.
* **Usage** — how often the metric is queried. Cheap, and what metrics-drilldown's badge already does.

These are different features with different costs. Nothing can be scoped until this is answered.

**2. A backend endpoint, if the answer is cardinality.**

Investigated during grafana/grafana#128774 and confirmed absent:

* The unmerged Prometheus Search API does not provide a count.
* metrics-drilldown does not provide one either.
* A real cardinality count needs a new `promlib` endpoint in `grafana-prometheus-datasource` — i.e. a backend change in another repo, on a different release cadence.

* Everything else in the sidebar row is done: the catalog fetch, batching, and metric → label keys → label values expansion all landed in grafana/grafana#128774.
* If the answer is *usage*, this is likely small and frontend-only. If it is *cardinality*, it needs its own backend ticket first.
* No count is rendered anywhere today, deliberately — a column that always reads empty is worse than an absent one.

Alerting: settings page fails to load external Alertmanager configuration when jira_configs receiver is defined

The Alertmanager Settings page fails to load with a 500 error when an external Prometheus Alertmanager has any `jira_configs` receiver defined:

Failed to load Alertmanager configuration
```
yaml: unmarshal errors:
  line 187: cannot unmarshal !!map into string
  line 189: cannot unmarshal !!map into string
```

[image]

The error is thrown server-side in `GettableStatus.UnmarshalJSON` ([alertmanager.go:434](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/main/pkg/services/ngalert/api/tooling/definitions/alertmanager.go)), which performs a second-pass YAML unmarshal of `amStatus.Config.Original` into `PostableApiReceiver`. Grafana's `JiraIntegration` struct types `summary` and `description` as `*string`, but Alertmanager applies defaults to those fields and serialises them back as nested objects:
```
summary:
  template: '{{ template "jira.default.summary" . }}'
description:
  template: '{{ template "jira.default.description" . }}'
```
The YAML unmarshaller cannot put a `!!map` into a `*string`, causing the unmarshal to fail and a 500 to be returned to the frontend. The fields field has the same latent issue (`*string` vs `map[string]any`), though it only manifests if fields is explicitly configured.

The upstream Alertmanager correctly types these as a `JiraFieldConfig` struct with a dual-form `UnmarshalYAML` that accepts both a plain string (legacy) and the full object form. Grafana's struct does not.

**Potential fix:**
`JiraIntegration.Summary` and `JiraIntegration.Description` in `pkg/services/ngalert/api/tooling/definitions/contact_points.go` should be changed from `*string` to a nested struct type matching the upstream `JiraFieldConfig` (see `notify/jira/config.go` in prometheus/alertmanager), with a dual-form `UnmarshalYAML` that accepts both a plain string (legacy) and the full object form.

The `Fields *string` field has the same issue and should become`map[string]any`. The failing unmarshal is at `alertmanager.go:434`

The Alertmanager Settings page should load successfully and display the configuration, including any `jira_configs` receivers — consistent with how other receiver types (Slack, OpsGenie, PagerDuty) are handled.

Unknown — Jira receiver support in external Alertmanager was introduced upstream in v0.27.0. The issue appears to be present since Grafana first attempted to support `jira_configs` for external Alertmanager instances.

1. Configure Grafana with an external Prometheus Alertmanager datasource (not Grafana-managed AM).
2. Ensure the Alertmanager has a `jira_configs` receiver block in its configuration — any valid `jira_configs` block will trigger this, because Alertmanager automatically populates `summary` and `description` with defaults even if omitted from the source config.
3. Navigate to Alerting → Settings -> Attempt to view configuration for alertmanager
4. Result: 500 error, page fails to load with `yaml: unmarshal errors: cannot unmarshal !!map into string.`

Workaround: Removing the `jira_configs` block (and its associated route/matcher) from the Alertmanager configuration allows the Settings page to load normally.

Allow embedding on a limited set of referrers

**Why is this needed**:
Currently, you can set allow_embedding to `true` to remove the `X-Frame-Options: deny` header so that Grafana dashboards can be embedded. However, this has the limitation of removing a useful clickjacking mitigation. Lifting the embed restriction only for certain referrers would allow for embedding when the location doing the embedding is trusted while still providing broader mitigation against clickjacking.

**What would you like to be added**:
It would be great to have a new option (or further flexibility for the existing allow_embedding option) such that `X-Frame-Options: deny` is conditionally provided depending on where the request originates from. For example, I may want to allow embedding a public dashboard hosted on grafana.example.com on an internal administration interface hosted on admin.example.com. This could also be achieved by allowing configuration of the Content-Security-Policy frame-ancestors directive.

I could do this myself by putting Grafana behind a separate reverse proxy, but it would simplify ensuring a secure setup by allowing this to be configurable within Grafana directly.

**Who is this feature for?**
This is intended for users who want to allow public embedding (particularly for public dashboards) in other parts of their internal systems without removing the entire security mitigation for clickjacking.

list Redis-compatible servers (Valkey, KiviDB) for [remote_cache], with measured numbers on tuned servers

**What would you like to be added?**

A short note in the `[remote_cache]` docs saying that Redis-protocol servers other than Redis work, such as Valkey and KiviDB, and what they change for large installs.

**Why is this needed?**

With `type = redis`, OAuth token sync and ID forwarding read the remote cache on every request, from every Grafana replica. The cache layer only issues `GET`, `SET EX` and `DEL` (`pkg/infra/remotecache/redis_storage.go`), so any Redis-compatible server works unchanged.

We replayed that mix (95% `GET`, 4% `SET EX 600`, 1% `DEL`, 1.5 KB values, 10k entries) on three servers. Each server got 4 dedicated cores, and memtier ran on 4 other cores. Redis and Valkey ran with `--io-threads 4`, KiviDB with `--threads 4`. Each server was started fresh and run twice, averages shown. The `DEL`s ran against a separate set of preloaded keys, so every `GET` was a hit.

| Connections | Redis 8.12 (`--io-threads 4`) | Valkey 9.0 (`--io-threads 4`) | KiviDB 1.2.2 (`--threads 4`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 48 | 232k ops/s | 260k | 290k (1.25x Redis) |
| 500 | 275k | 267k | 330k (1.20x Redis) |

- **Memory for the dataset:** about 18 MiB on all three, so no difference.

To try it, run one worker thread per core: `docker run -d -p 6379:6380 kividb/kividb:v1.2.2 --threads <cores> --requirepass <pw>`. Today's default uses half the cores, and a fix for that is in progress.

KiviDB is an open-source (AGPLv3), multi-threaded Redis-protocol server written in Rust. The full harness is available on request. Happy to send a docs PR if you'd like one.

Edit: the first version of this table ran Redis with io-threads off and showed 2.7-3.0x. It now uses Redis with `--io-threads 4`, same as Valkey.

Runtime: Resolve API availability and versions through API discovery

**Parent:** #114536

**Frontend code that calls `/apis` hardcodes the API group and version, and assumes the API is there. The server is never asked.**

- [`getApiVersion()`](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/main/packages/grafana-runtime/src/services/pluginUtils.ts#L3) always returns `v0alpha1`
  - used by plugin settings, plugin metas, app plugin health, `callAppPluginProxy` and `callDataSourcePluginProxy`
- [The MT cache source for datasources](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/main/packages/grafana-runtime/src/services/dataSource/sources/mt/api.ts) hardcodes `v0alpha1`
- Generated RTK clients use a fixed `BASE_URL`
- Feature flags decide whether a new API is used
  - if the group isn't served (OSS, an older version, a tenant without the plugin), the caller finds out from a failed request
- Features run their own discovery logic, each with its own request and cache
  - dashboards
  - folders
  - alert rules
  - annotations
  - library panels
  - provisioning
  - live panel
  - query library
  - data source settings save (`DatasourceAPIVersions`)
  - stars (#136105, open)

- **MT:** [the router can show each tenant only the groups it may see](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/pull/136246) (the per-namespace filter is still a no-op). Feature flags can't tell us this.
- **Unblocks the delivery plan:** the [query caching join](https://github.com/grafana/grafana-enterprise/issues/14345) needs to know if `querycaching.grafana.app` is served.
- **Plugins:** lets teams use their own fetch utilities instead of one wrapper function per endpoint.
- **One implementation:** a page that loads several features sends 4–5 discovery requests today.

**A discovery service in `@grafana/runtime`**, exported from the stable `@grafana/runtime` entry point and tagged `@alpha` until the API settles. Plugins use it through `@grafana/plugin-compat`, which forwards to the runtime when it has the export and falls back to its own `GET /apis/<group>/` on older Grafana versions.
- reports what the server serves (groups, versions, resources) and builds base URLs
- it **doesn't make the requests** or choose the legacy fallback; callers keep their own clients.

- **Fetching:** plain `GET /apis` once per page load. If the root request fails, fall back to `GET /apis/<group>/`. Concurrent callers share one request. It never blocks first paint and never runs without a session.
- **Invalidation:** the cache is dropped when a plugin is installed, updated, uninstalled, enabled or disabled.

More info on the service in #137724.

Coauthoring: Prevent stale Query Coauthoring adapters after query or datasource switches

PanelEditNext can reuse QueryEditorPanel while its keyed datasource editor remounts. The previous editor unregisters its coauthoring adapter in a passive effect, leaving a render window where Core could read the old adapter with the new query row or datasource host.

Review context: [https://github.com/grafana/grafana/pull/131166#discussion_r3872683639](<https://github.com/grafana/grafana/pull/131166#discussion_r3872683639>)

* Bind each registered adapter to the datasource-instance/query-row identity and the current registrar generation.
* Render and transact with the adapter only while that registration matches the current row and coauthoring remains eligible.
* Fail closed immediately when switching query rows or datasources, without waiting for datasource effect cleanup.
* Add regression coverage for switching query refs and leaving the eligible datasource.
* Document the adapter identity invariant and the post-refactor ownership/lifecycle in CONTEXT.md.

* A previous row's adapter is never read or rendered with the next row's host.
* Switching away from Prometheus cannot leave the previous coauthoring surface mounted.
* Datasource cleanup remains responsible for disposing its editor-side resources.
* Focused tests, lint, formatting, and diff hygiene pass.

Coauthoring: Handle time-range and variable changes during query-coauthoring preview

During a staged query-coauthoring preview, PanelEditNext runs the proposed query through an isolated `SceneQueryRunner` clone while the canonical runner retains the baseline query. A time-range or template-variable change can rerun the canonical baseline and replace the projected proposal data while the coauthoring surface still says it is previewing the proposal.

Keep the coauthoring state, editor contents, and panel data truthful when query context changes during an active proposal.

Invalidate the active proposal when the canonical query context changes:

* dispose the isolated preview
* restore the baseline panel data
* dismiss the coauthoring session
* do not make another Assistant request
* do not introduce a second active query-runner writer or a duplicate query run

This is intentionally safer and lighter than transparently rerunning the proposal against the new context.

* Changing the panel time range cannot leave baseline results under a proposal-preview state.
* Changing a template variable, ad hoc filter, or scope has the same safe invalidation behavior.
* Preview-authored panel-data projection does not invalidate itself.
* Disposal is idempotent and restores the exact baseline query and panel data.
* Invalidation does not issue another Assistant request or duplicate query run.
* Focused `queryPreview`, `QueryEditorRenderer`, and `QueryCoauthoring` tests cover the lifecycle.
* The PanelEditNext flow is validated with `agent-browser`.

Should invalidation close immediately, or briefly explain that query context changed? Transparently rerunning the proposal remains out of scope unless preview writer ownership is redesigned.

Query Editor: Guard loadDatasource against concurrent datasource switches

`PanelDataPaneNext.loadDatasource` has no generation guard, so with two loads in flight the **slower one wins** and leaves the pane desynced from the query runner.

`loadDatasource` awaits `getDataSourceInstance`, then `getDataSourceInstanceSettings`, then unconditionally calls `this.setState({ datasource, dsSettings, dsError: undefined })` and `storeLastUsedDataSourceInLocalStorage(...)`. There's no in-flight token compared before the `setState`.

Two concurrent invocations are reachable: `onActivate` kicks off `resolveDatasourceRef().then(ref => this.loadDatasource(ref))` while the query-runner subscription also calls `loadDatasource()` on datasource changes.

To reproduce: switch from datasource A to B where B's plugin bundle isn't yet imported (slow), then switch back to A while B is still loading. A resolves fast from `pluginCache`, then B's load completes and overwrites it. Result: `dsSettings` says B while `queryRunner.state.datasource` says A — and B gets written to the last-used-datasource localStorage key.

Let's add a monotonic counter on the scene object, captured at the top of `loadDatasource` and compared before each `setState` (and before the localStorage write), bailing out if a newer load has started.

Note the React-side hook does **not** have this problem — `useQueryDatasource` uses `useAsync` from `react-use`, which guards with `lastCallId` and `useMountedState`. Only the scene object is affected, so this is a good template for what the fix should achieve.

Unrelated to the React 19 adoption work; filed here because it surfaced during that review.

Transformations: Help drawer shows stale docs after switching transformation

The transformation help drawer can show one transformation's title above another's documentation.

To reproduce:

1. Select the **Organize fields** transformation and open its help.
2. Close the drawer.
3. Select **Reduce** and open its help.

The drawer title says "Reduce" while the body still shows Organize-fields documentation, until the new docs promise resolves.

In `TransformationHelpDisplay`, `helpHtml` is `useState` seeded with the fallback markdown and only ever written from the resolved promise — it is **never reset when** `registryItem` **changes**. Meanwhile the drawer title reads live from `selectedTransformation.registryItem.name`. So during the load window the title is current and the body is one transformation behind.

The effect's `cancelled` guard is correct and is not the problem here; this is a missing reset, not a race.

The cheap fix is to reset `helpHtml` when the transformer id changes — either clear to the loading/fallback state in the effect before fetching, or key the component on the id.

Alternatively this is fixed by construction as part of loading the docs with `use()` (tracked in the React 19 work), since `use()` reads the value and the identity it belongs to in the same render. That refactor is the tidier end state, but let's not hold this bug hostage to it — the reset is a couple of lines and can ship independently.

Query Editor: Replace hand-rolled useEffectEvent patterns

`PanelEditNext` contains **four hand-rolled implementations of** `useEffectEvent` — the ref + render-phase write + `useCallback([], …)` delegator pattern — written before the API was available to us:

* `useSelectionState` — **seven** latest-value refs, six of which exist purely so the returned mutators can read fresh props without listing them as deps. All eight `.current =` assignments happen *during render*, which the React docs explicitly forbid and which is unsafe under a discarded or replayed render.
* `QueryEditorContextWrapper` — a `clearSideEffectsRef` + `useCallback(() => ref.current(), [])` delegator + a render-phase write, spread across 170 lines, existing only to break a declaration-order cycle.
* `useStackedItemScroll` — carries a comment that paraphrases the `useEffectEvent` docs almost verbatim.
* `hooks.ts` (`useRatioResize`) — three refs so the `pointerdown` listener isn't detached and re-attached on every `pointermove` frame during a drag.

There's also one genuine bug in the family: `useActiveStackedItemObserver` lists `onActiveItemChange` in its deps only to satisfy the linter, with a comment saying the intended trigger is `itemsKey`. If that callback's identity churns, the `IntersectionObserver` is rebuilt, its `visibleItems` map is discarded, and the recomputed dominant section can differ — yanking the user's selection mid-scroll.

Two verified facts make adoption **net-negative today**. Both are reproducible; see the parent for the exact commands.

1. `eslint-plugin-react-hooks@5.2.0` **has** `useEffectEvent` **support compiled out** — `isUseEffectEventIdentifier(node) { return false; }` in both shipped bundles. Since `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` is `'error'` for us, the hook's result is reported as a **missing dependency**.
2. **React 19.2's** `useEffectEvent` **returns a fresh closure every render** — only the inner `ref.impl` is stable. So satisfying the linter by adding it to deps makes the effect re-run *every render*: the exact opposite of the goal.

Net effect: we'd trade each ref for an `eslint-disable-next-line`, in a directory that currently has exactly **one** such disable. That's worse, not better.

It would also silently regress the call sites that depend on callback **identity** stability — a contract documented in a comment in `QueryEditorContextWrapper` explaining that these callbacks are hoisted out of `uiState` precisely so consumers' dep arrays don't re-fire. `useEffectEvent` does not preserve identity.

A bump of `eslint-plugin-react-hooks` from `5.2.0` to `7.1.1`, which ships the compiler-backed rule set. That's a repo-wide change with its own blast radius and is a frontend-platform decision, not ours — let's raise it as an ask rather than proposing it here.

Worth noting for whoever picks this up: [`useStableCallback`](<https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/main/packages/grafana-ui/src/components/CodeMirror/useStableProps.ts>) already exists in `@grafana/ui` and is the **better** tool for the identity-sensitive sites, because it preserves identity where `useEffectEvent` does not. Its "until we are off React 18" comment is stale, but its behaviour is still the one those call sites want. Migrating the four sites there is a viable alternative that needs no eslint bump.

**None, deliberately.** This has no user-visible delta — the payoff is removing 4 hand-rolled implementations and 12+ render-phase ref writes, plus fixing the `useActiveStackedItemObserver` selection bug. A before/after recording here would be padding. The `useActiveStackedItemObserver` fix is the one piece with observable behaviour and could be split out and shipped on its own merits.

Transformations: Load help docs with use() behind a Suspense boundary

`TransformationHelpDisplay` loads its docs with the classic `useEffect` + `setState` + cancellation-flag pattern. The cancellation guard is correct, but there's a separate bug it can't prevent: `helpHtml` **is never reset when** `registryItem` **changes.** The drawer title reads live from `selectedTransformation.registryItem.name` while the body still holds the *previous* transformation's docs until the new promise resolves, so the title and body disagree.

[`use()`](<https://react.dev/reference/react/use>) eliminates this class of bug by construction, because the value and the identity it belongs to are read in the same render.

* Add a module-level `Map<string, Promise<...>>` cache around `getTransformationContent` for stable promise identity. `use()` needs a cached promise — one created during render loops forever. ~4 lines, and since the content is immutable per transformer id there's no invalidation problem. Fold `renderMarkdown` and the `FALLBACK_DOCS_LINK` catch into the cached promise so graceful degradation is preserved.

Query Editor: Show datasource changes optimistically in the query picker

Changing a query's datasource is one of only **two** genuinely async mutations in this editor, and today the UI gives no feedback for the whole round trip.

`PanelDataPaneNext.changeDataSource` awaits up to four async calls before it touches state — two `getDataSourceInstanceSettings` lookups, a `getDataSourceInstance` (which can trigger a plugin module `import()`), and another settings lookup on the Mixed-mode transition. Meanwhile the picker still renders the **old** datasource, because `ContentHeader` derives `current` from resolved settings rather than from what you just clicked. The sidebar card logo lags in lockstep.

In practical terms, clicking "Loki" on a cold plugin load looks like: picker still says "Prometheus" → pane blanks to `Loading datasource` → Loki finally appears. And if it fails, the UI just stays on the old datasource with no explanation.

Let's use [`useOptimistic`](<https://react.dev/reference/react/useOptimistic>) so the picker and card logo flip immediately and revert automatically on failure. The picker already hands us a full `DataSourceInstanceSettings` in its `onChange`, so the optimistic value is available at click time.

Two call sites:

* `changeDataSource` — needs a prerequisite refactor: the promise is currently **dropped on the floor** in `QueryEditorContextWrapper`, which wraps `dataPane.changeDataSource(...)` in a non-async arrow and discards the result. `useOptimistic` can't know an action is in flight until that promise is returned.
* `bulkChangeDataSource` — the cheaper retrofit, since `useBulkActions` already awaits it properly. There's no pending affordance today: the `DataSourceModal` stays open and interactive through a `Promise.all` of per-query settings lookups plus a plugin load, so a double-click fires it twice.

**Explicitly not in scope:** every other mutator. Scene `setState` is synchronous — 18 of ~20 mutators on `PanelDataPaneNext` commit immediately, so there is no in-flight window and `useOptimistic` would be pure indirection. That includes drag-reorder, rename, delete, duplicate, hide, and all the bulk toggles. The `usePending*` hooks are also **not** optimistic UI despite the name; "pending" there means "a type picker is open".

`changeDataSource` may legitimately not apply the picked datasource verbatim in Mixed mode. Confirm that reverting-to-truth is the behaviour we want there, rather than a silent divergence between what the user picked and what landed.

2. Then force a failure (point a query at a deleted datasource uid) to show the revert.

**Before:** picker shows the old datasource for the entire round trip; on failure, nothing changes and nothing is said. **After:** flips immediately, reverts with an error on failure.

This is the biggest user-visible win available from React 19 in `PanelEditNext`, and the one with the most uncertainty — so let's spike it rather than scope it blind.

* Plugin editor mount count per switch (expect N → 0 on revisit).
* Datasource resolutions per switch — `queryDsLoading` flips today on every `refId` change.

Query Editor: Adopt React 19 features in PanelEditNext

As [announced in Slack](<https://raintank-corp.slack.com/archives/C03E2AQKU2W/p1786630264164759>), core is fully migrated to React 19 and the feature flag is gone. Four new APIs are now fair game: [`use`](<https://react.dev/reference/react/use>), [`useOptimistic`](<https://react.dev/reference/react/useOptimistic>), [`useEffectEvent`](<https://react.dev/reference/react/useEffectEvent>), and [`<Activity>`](<https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity>).

Let's work out where they genuinely pay off in `PanelEditNext` rather than adopting all four on principle. This issue carries the assessment; the sub-issues carry the work.

`<Activity>` **is where the value is.** The other three are each constrained by something concrete — two by verified blockers, one by our architecture.

| API | Verdict | Why |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `<Activity>` | **Adopt** | The editor destroys local `useState` on every view switch — collapsed sections, picker search/filter, and the datasource plugin's own editor instance. 3 sites, sub-issues 1–3. |
| `useOptimistic` | **Narrow — 2 sites** | Scene mutations are *synchronous*. 18 of ~20 mutators on `PanelDataPaneNext` are plain `setState`, so there's no in-flight window to be optimistic about. Only `changeDataSource` and `bulkChangeDataSource` touch the network. Sub-issue 4. |
| `use()` | **1 site, behind a new boundary** | There is no `<Suspense>` between `GrafanaRoute` and this tree, so suspending today blanks the whole dashboard. Sub-issue 5. |
| `useEffectEvent` | **Blocked** | Our `eslint-plugin-react-hooks` doesn't support it, and adopting anyway would regress identity-stability contracts. Sub-issue 6. |

Note that `PanelEditNext` would be the **first adopter of** `<Activity>`**,** `useOptimistic`**, and** `useEffectEvent` **anywhere in** `grafana/grafana` — no other first-party usage exists in `public/` or `packages/`. We'd be setting the precedent, so sub-issue 1 is deliberately the smallest possible change.

Recorded here so no sub-issue has to re-derive it. All four are reproducible from a clean checkout.

**1. All four APIs are stable in our installed React** (`react@19.2.8`) — no `unstable_`/`experimental_` prefix:

```
node -e "const R=require('react'); console.log(typeof R.useEffectEvent, typeof R.Activity, typeof R.useOptimistic, typeof R.use)"
# function symbol function function
```

`@types/react@19.2.18` declares `Activity: ExoticComponent<ActivityProps>` with `mode?: 'hidden' | 'visible'`.

**2.** `eslint-plugin-react-hooks@5.2.0` **has** `useEffectEvent` **support compiled out:**

```
grep -A2 "function isUseEffectEventIdentifier" node_modules/eslint-plugin-react-hooks/cjs/*.js
# function isUseEffectEventIdentifier(node) { return false; }
```

The plumbing exists (the `useEffectEventFunctions` WeakSet, the "must not be included in the dependency array" message) but every gate is dead. Since `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` is `'error'` for us, the hook's result gets reported as a **missing dependency**.

**3.** `useEffectEvent` **returns a fresh closure every render** — only the inner `ref.impl` is stable:

```
grep -A12 "function updateEvent" node_modules/react-dom/cjs/react-dom-client.development.js
```

Combined with (2): satisfying the linter by adding it to deps makes the effect re-run *every render* — the exact opposite of the point.

**4. No** `<Suspense>` **boundary above this tree.** The nearest is [`GrafanaRoute.tsx`](<https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/main/public/app/core/navigation/GrafanaRoute.tsx>), whose fallback is a whole-page `<PageLoader />`. Trace: `GrafanaRoute` → `DashboardScenePage` → `DashboardSceneRenderer` → `PanelEditor` → `PanelEditorRendererNext` → `VizAndDataPaneNext` → `QueryEditorContent`, with nothing in between. `TransformationEditor` is the one place that does it right (`ErrorBoundaryAlert` + `Suspense`) and is our template.

Each sub-issue names, in its own **Evidence** section, what will demonstrate the benefit. Three tiers, matched to what the change actually is:

* **Before/after screen recordings** for the state-preservation and perceived-latency wins, where the delta is obvious on sight. These double as the `## Demo` section the PR template already expects.
* **Measurement** for sub-issue 3 only, because it's the one item where the benefit is a magnitude *and* the cost is real. It includes a counter-measurement (render cost of hidden-but-mounted editors) — publishing the cost alongside the benefit is what makes the benefit credible.
* **Nothing**, stated plainly, for sub-issue 6 — it has no user-visible delta and a manufactured demo would be padding.

* **Converting** `useQueryDatasource` **to** `use()`**.** It's already race-safe (`useAsync` guards with `lastCallId`), and converting means a custom `cacheKeyFn` over `ScopedVars`, replicating the legacy `DataSourceSrv` fallback inside a cached promise, and collapsing three distinct error alerts into one boundary. Net loss of UX fidelity.
* **Converting the** `usePending*` **hooks to** `useOptimistic`**.** Despite the name, "pending" there means "a type picker is currently open" — there are no promises involved. Same for drag-reorder, rename, delete, duplicate, and hide: all synchronous scene mutations.
* **Conditional** `use(Context)`**.** No viable site — all 7 accessors in `QueryEditorContext.tsx` read then throw, so nothing is conditional.
* **Bumping** `eslint-plugin-react-hooks`**.** Real, but a frontend-platform decision with repo-wide blast radius. See sub-issue 6.

PanelEditNext: query editor shows resolved datasource but query runs against the default (display/execution split)

In the new query editor (PanelEditNext / `PanelDataPaneNext`), a panel whose query has **no explicit datasource** shows the *resolved* datasource (last-used from localStorage, else the configured default) in the editor, but query **execution** still goes through the queryRunner — whose datasource is null and therefore resolves to the configured **default**. The datasource the editor displays and the datasource the query actually runs against disagree.

* You can build a query in the shown datasource's editor (e.g. a PromQL query in a Prometheus builder), hit **Run**, and silently get results from the **default** datasource (e.g. TestData) with **no warning**.
* Confined to **edit-mode** of **no-datasource** panels.
* **No data corruption:** saving an untouched panel keeps the datasource null; the rendered dashboard runs the default correctly.
* Severity: **low**.

`PanelDataPaneNext.onActivate` → `resolveDatasourceRef()` resolves a datasource ref for panels with no explicit datasource (priority: last-used from localStorage, else configured default), and `loadDatasource()` sets `dsSettings` from it — which is what renders the query editor.

But `resolveDatasourceRef` **deliberately does not write back to the queryRunner** (to avoid persisting a datasource onto a panel that was saved without one). So query execution continues to use `queryRunner.state.datasource` (null → default). The datasource shown by the editor therefore never governs what the query actually runs against — a display/execution split.

Add a transformation that rewrites cell values via regex (not just field names)

There's a gap in the table-panel transformations: nothing rewrites the **values inside cells**, only field names or types.

This kept biting me trying to join two data sources that have the same logical key formatted slightly differently.

Table panel with two queries:

- **Query A** — Loki, returns rows with a column `session_id` containing values like `pv_019dc8a7deae7a73beed303d2f7f135e` (plain string).
- **Query B** — Tempo TraceQL metric, returns label values as `"pv_019dc8a7deae7a73beed303d2f7f135e"` (with literal `"` characters wrapping the value — that's a separate issue at grafana/tempo, but my point here is broader).

To join them, I'd want a transformation that strips the leading/trailing quotes from every cell in the `session_id` column on B before the `joinByField` runs. Roughly:

```
field:    session_id
match:    ^"|"$
replace:  
```

…and that's the whole thing. Two-line transformation, applied per-row.

Walked through every transformation in the dropdown:

| Transformation | Why it doesn't fit |
|---|---|
| `renameByRegex` | Renames the field (column header), not the cells inside it. |
| `convertFieldType` | Changes type (string → number, etc.), values stay the same. |
| `calculateField` (binary) | Math operations only — no string ops. |
| `Filter fields by name` | Drops/keeps columns wholesale. |
| `Organize fields` | Reorders / hides — doesn't touch values. |
| `Series to rows` / `Rows to series` | Structural pivot, no rewrite. |
| `Group by` / `Reduce` | Aggregation, not per-cell rewrite. |

The closest community workaround I've seen is forking the data source to mutate the response before it reaches the transformation pipeline — heavy for what's effectively `value.replace(re, replacement)`.

The Tempo-quotes case is what made me hit it, but I've wanted this before for:

- Stripping a trailing slash from URL paths so `Loki: /foo/` joins with `Tempo: /foo`
- Lowercasing user emails before joining (one source has `User@example.com`, the other `user@example.com`)
- Removing a fixed prefix like `service-` before grouping
- Normalising IP addresses to a `/24` block

All of these come up in real dashboards joining two data sources. Today the answer is "use a different data source layout" or "write a custom plugin", neither of which is great.

A new transformation, maybe called `Replace values by regex` or `Modify values`, in the standard list with these inputs:

- **Field** — the column to operate on (single field, no glob)
- **Match** — regex string
- **Replace with** — replacement string (with `$1` / `$2` capture group support)
- **Apply to** — `All rows` (default) / `Only matching rows`

The implementation is small — most of the work is the UI surface and discoverability through the transformation list, not the actual replace logic.

If a full transformation is too much:

- An option in `calculateField` to support string `replace(field, regex, replacement)` as a function
- An option in `convertFieldType` for "string with regex strip" — e.g. quoted-string-to-string

- Grafana: 11.6.0
- Use case is dashboard table panels (not Explore — Explore can do more via expressions)

Happy to test a PR if anyone takes this on. If there's an existing issue I missed, point me at it and I'll close this one.

Thanks!

Add Pivot transformation

**Why is this needed**:

The long story is available in this Grafana Forum [post](https://community.grafana.com/t/time-series-how-to-use-column-values-as-serie-names/159341).

To sum up, it would be very convenient to have a transformation that would transform SQL query output to format expected by `Time Series` (one column per serie), but, unlike `Grouping to Matrix`, will keep other columns (metadata) intact:

| Year | Serie | Value | Report | | Year | Report | Revenue | Profit | Taxes |
| ---- | ------- | ----- | ------------- | ---- | ---- | ------------- | ------- | ------ | ----- |
| 2024 | Revenue | 100 | 2024.xls | | 2024 | 2024.xls | 100 | | |
| 2024 | Profit | 10 | 2024.xls | | 2024 | 2024.xls | | 10 | |
| 2024 | Taxes | 20 | 2024.xls | --> | 2024 | 2024.xls | | | 20 |
| 2025 | Revenue | 120 | 2025-rev.xlsx | | 2025 | 2025-rev.xlsx | 120 | | |
| 2025 | Profit | 5 | 2025-pft.xlsx | | 2025 | 2025-pft.xlsx | | 5 | |
| 2025 | Taxes | 30 | 2025-tax.xlsx | | 2025 | 2025-tax.xlsx | | | 30 |

**What would you like to be added**:

I've prepared such [pivot transformation](https://github.com/sknaumov/grafana/commits/sknaumov/pivot-transformation-11.6.8/) for Grafana v11.6.8, but currently have no throughput to port it to upstream.

I've used `Grouping to Matrix` transformation implementation as a reference.

**Who is this feature for?**

Anyone who uses `Time Series` visualization but have SQL query that returns serie name in a column instead of having multiple columns with per-serie data.

Moreover, it fixes multiple issues visible with alternative `json_object_agg` + `Extract Fields` transformation approach:
1. All points of a serie are connected regardless of settings. With my `Pivot` transformation they are connected this way only if `Connect null values - always` is set.
2. When hovering over a graph, for `json_object_agg` + `Extract Fields` way values for ALL series are displayed. It makes this hovering summary unusable when there are a lot of series. With `Pivot` transformation only the values of series defined for the time point I hover over are displayed.

OpenID Connect .well-known for simpler configuration

**Why is this needed**:

Most IAMs that support OIDC/OAUTH support a [discovery endpoint](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8414) that allows clients to get important information about the IAM, such as the issuer name, token and auth URLs, etc. This greatly simplifies the configuration process. While support for this was added via the auth configuration form in the UI as mentioned in #27443, there still seems to be no way to utilize the discover URL through the TOML configuration file. According to the [announcement](https://grafana.com/whats-new/2024-09-24-openid-connect-discovery-url-for-generic-oauth/), it only appears to be supported via the form in the UI.

**What would you like to be added**:

The [OAUTH Configurations](https://grafana.com/whats-new/2024-09-24-openid-connect-discovery-url-for-generic-oauth/) would be expanded to support the discover URL. When set, it will no longer be required to manually set the token, auth, and api URLs.

**Who is this feature for?**

Any user using OIDC or OAUTH 2.0 who wants to configure auth in Grafana via the TOML configuration files.

Dashboards: inefficiencies in client-side transformations

**SLACK Thread**: based on discussion https://grafana.slack.com/archives/C0Y4TLW74/p1742891364051639 with [debug-Duration-2025-03-25 18_36_59.json.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19468241/debug-Duration-2025-03-25.18_36_59.json.txt)

How can we tackle the inefficiencies that cause client-side transformations in Grafana to block the browser tab?

**TL;DR:**
The client-side transformation significantly burdens laptop/desktop CPUs due to extensive RAM copy operations. This not only blocks the browser tab for several seconds (or even minutes) but also repeatedly recalculates the same data, resulting in a non-responsive dashboard that frustrates users.
Dashboard panel / Case: "Show percentile of duration of tasks grouped by 3-hour intervals for a selected time period."

**Workflow Details:**
Data Retrieval:
* The Loki query returns duration values for each task_id in 3-hour groups.
* This query step performs well, with a 12-hour range typically taking about 0.2 seconds to process and caching effectively.
* The result is a list of metrics, for example: `[ { "metric": { "task_id": "xxxx" }, "values": [ [ 1742850000, "10099" ] ] }, ... ]`

_Transformation Process in Grafana UI:_
* Merge series/tables.
* Change the task_id column name to duration.
* Calculate count, max, 50th percentile, and 95th percentile.

**Performance Comparison (Query vs. Transformation, with browser unresponsiveness):**
* For a 12-hour period (~17k metrics)
```
Loki Query time ~0.2 s
Grafana UI: ~8 s
```
* For a 24-hour period (~43k metrics)
```
Loki Query time ~0.5 s
Grafana UI: ~58 s
```
(Browser reports "tab is not responding," leading to user panic.)

* For a 48-hour period (~72k metrics):
```
Loki Query time: ~1 s
Grafana: ~3 minutes
```
* For a 96-hour period (~133k metrics):
```
Loki Query time: ~4 s
Grafana: ~18 minutes
```

**User Impact:**
Users often require trend analysis over longer periods (such as 7 days, 30 days, or even 3 months). However, the current implementation of client-side transformations is unable to efficiently handle these larger datasets. With a 2-day period taking up to 3 minutes of CPU time, the entire dashboard tab becomes blocked, and there is no progress indicator. Consequently, users may refresh the page mid-calculation, triggering redundant computations and causing further delays. Additionally, the high CPU load results in the laptop/desktop fan running at maximum speed to manage the heat.
It would be beneficial if the system could handle longer tasks in the background while providing incremental updates through a panel. This would prevent the browser tab from freezing and enhance the overall user experience. But that is not happening.

Any suggestions on improving the panel, query, or transformation? Has anyone experienced similar issues?

mysql: improve backslash-handling in dashboard variables

if you want to use a dashboard-variable in a query, and the variable-value contains a backlash, it will not be handled correctly.
for example:
- you have a table (`t1`) with a `name` field, that contains the value `tw\o` (4 characters).
- you create a dashboard variable, name=`v1`, type=custom, with two values: `tw\o` and `tw\\o`.
- now write a query like this: `select name from t1 where name='$v1'`
- if you choose the variable-value `tw\o`, this returns 0 rows
- if you choose the variable-value `tw\\o`, this returns 1 row

we should look into improving this (so that the value `tw\o` finds the database-row.

complications:
- we have to be careful, someone may already be working around this problem by duplicating the backslashes, and us escaping the backslash might break such dashboards (but it may be the right thing to do, needs investigation).
- the rules change when the variable is interpolated into a regular expression

the mysql-database behavior also slightly changes based on the value of the [NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/sql-mode.html#sqlmode_no_backslash_escapes) setting, ideally we should find a solution that works always, regardless of this settings's value.

Dashboards: Restore missing variable reorder, annotation reorder, and dashboard copy events

Three dashboard interaction events have reporting helpers but are not emitted by the current UI paths:

- `dashboards_variables_reordered`
- `dashboards_annotations_reordered`
- `grafana_dashboard_copied`

The underlying actions remain supported, so missing events can make usage appear stale even when users perform these actions. These findings come from source inspection, rather than production telemetry.

**Variable reordering**

`DashboardInteractions.variablesReordered({ source: 'edit_pane' })` exists but has no callers. The sidebar's `DashboardVariablesList` uses `createDragEndHandler`, which updates variable order through an undoable edit without reporting the interaction.

- [Tracking helper](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/81c267ef42c/public/app/features/dashboard-scene/utils/interactions.ts#L164-L168)
- [Current drag handler](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/81c267ef42c/public/app/features/dashboard-scene/sidebar/dashboard/variableListActions.ts#L85-L143)

**Annotation reordering**

`DashboardInteractions.annotationsReordered({ source: 'edit_pane' })` also has no callers. `DashboardAnnotationsList.onDragEnd` updates annotation order through an undoable edit without reporting the interaction.

- [Tracking helper](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/81c267ef42c/public/app/features/dashboard-scene/utils/interactions.ts#L199-L203)
- [Current drag handler](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/81c267ef42c/public/app/features/dashboard-scene/sidebar/dashboard/DashboardAnnotationsList.tsx#L54-L109)

**Saving a dashboard copy**

`SaveDashboardAsForm` calls `useSaveDashboard(false)`, while submitting `saveAsCopy: true` in the save options. The hook decides whether to emit `grafana_dashboard_copied` using its separate `isCopy` argument, not the submitted option. As a result, successful copies follow the created/saved tracking branch. All production callers of this hook currently pass `false`.

The existing hook-level coverage in `DashboardModes.test.tsx` passes `true` explicitly for copy cases, so it does not catch the form-to-hook wiring problem. The same flag also controls the edit-period outcome (`saved_as_copy` versus `saved`).

- [Form hook argument](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/81c267ef42c/public/app/features/dashboard-scene/saving/SaveDashboardAsForm.tsx#L65)
- [Submitted copy option](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/81c267ef42c/public/app/features/dashboard-scene/saving/SaveDashboardAsForm.tsx#L134-L146)
- [Tracking branch](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/81c267ef42c/public/app/features/dashboard-scene/saving/useSaveDashboard.ts#L103-L118)

With interaction reporting observed or mocked in the current dashboard UI:

1. Enter dashboard edit mode and reorder two editable variables in the sidebar.
2. Reorder two annotation queries in the sidebar.
3. Use **Save as copy** on an existing dashboard and complete the save successfully.

The corresponding events listed above are not reported by these paths.

Transformations: Add field from calculation drops frames when "Replace all fields" is on and the input field is missing

When "Replace all fields" is enabled in the Add field from calculation transformation, any frame in which the calculation can't find its input field is removed from the result entirely, including its time field and all of its other fields. This affects Binary operation, Unary operation, Cumulative functions, Window functions and Template modes, and shows up with multiple queries whose frames don't all contain the referenced field: those series silently disappear from the panel instead of being left unchanged, which reads as missing data rather than as a transformation that didn't apply to them.

1. Create a panel with two TestData queries using the CSV content scenario: query A with `name,value` and a row `a,1`, query B with `host,count` and a row `x,2`.
2. Switch to Table view.
3. Add the "Add field from calculation" transformation, choose Unary operation, and select the `value` field.
4. Turn on "Replace all fields".

Expressions: Info icons in the + Expression menu are not keyboard accessible

The description is available when the option has focus, for example as the menu item's accessible description.

Expose it through `Menu.Item` as `aria-describedby` pointing at a hidden element (small `MenuItem` + `ExpressionTypeDropdown` change).

Instrument SQL function usage in SQL Expressions

Let's add some more metrics to get a clear picture of which functions are being used in SQL Expressions, before we hit the allowlist. This should help with at least a few of things:

* Discovering which SQL features our users are trying to use, that haven't yet been added to the allowlist but could be good candidates for adding to the allowlist
* Understanding how often our users attempt to use a function that's been intentionally excluded from the allowlist
* In general, improve our understanding of how our users are using SQL Expressions..."how many users are doing joins?" etc.

Of course, we'll need to do this in a way that respects users' privacy. No collection of column names, etc.

Add base conversion / numeric encoding functions to SQL Expressions

To enable use cases like the one described in [https://github.com/grafana/grafana/issues/104140](<https://github.com/grafana/grafana/issues/104140>), we could add [HEX](<https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/string-functions.html#function_hex>) and some of its companions (`"hex", "unhex", "to_base64", "bin", "oct"`) to the [allowlist](<https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/9e147096843232f21a81801cb62493163a748fee/pkg/expr/sql/parser_allow.go#L182-L313>) of SQL functions.

We'd also want to add test cases in `parser_allow_test.go` to the `example_many_more_allowed_functions` query to cover the new functions.

No-Data Panel Handling-query/expression layer

**Why is this needed**:

Query returns no data, downstream calculations break. Enterprise customers building multi-query dashboards use expressions and transformations that chain off other query results. When one query returns no data, the entire chain collapses — value mappings and transforms don’t help because they run after all queries complete. The panel shows nothing, and any dependent alert or expression also returns no data. Customers need the query evaluation layer to emit a fallback value (typically zero) so the rest of the panel can still function.

**What would you like to be added**:

A Grafana user building a dashboard for any audience — technical or not — can configure what panels display when data is absent. Downstream calculations don’t collapse when one query returns empty. Scope: Have a configurable “no data fallback” option to the Reduce Expression (and/or as a new expression type). When a query or referenced expression returns no data, the Reduce Expression emits the configured fallback value (default: no change from current behaviour). This fallback is evaluated before downstream expressions run.

SQL Expressions datasource support

As captured in [Product DNA: Project: SQL Expressions DS Support](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1lO1wofbjtTho2CPNejFgP0oxKSKhEnej8RQ2Kla9TbM/edit?tab=t.2lecoimj8n8e), a major obstacle with SQL Expressions is knowing which data sources are supported. Currently, there are a couple of documentation resources:
- https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/visualizations/panels-visualizations/query-transform-data/sql-expressions/#compatible-data-sources
- https://grafana.com/developers/plugin-tools/how-to-guides/data-source-plugins/sql-requirements

, but these are inherently difficult to discover. The Grafana Developers doc is a helpful technical resource, but it's a lot for the average SQL Expressions practitioner to digest.

This epic captures the tasks related to providing in-app feedback about which datasources are fully supported by SQL expressions, categorically unsupported, or partially supported. In the case of partial support, we should make it clear to users (and agents, like Grafana Assistant) what the caveats are, and how to work around them.
